items.title: Hong Kong comics scene: Creators turning to AI in bid to recapture industry's heyday
items.excerpt: Hong Kong was once a comic powerhouse, producing titles that sold millions of copies each year. But while creators still win awards, sales are a fraction of what they used to be. Jeraldine Yap reports.
items.rationale: Fresh on-the-ground report of Hong Kong comic creators adopting AI in production; new region and use case not covered in history.

items.title: EWC denounces AI Tech's practice of shredding books and calls on Europe's decision-makers to take a firm stand
items.excerpt: The EWC condemns the AI tech practice of « destructively scanning » millions of old or rare European books and calls upon decision-makers and the whole of our European society to speak up loudly on behalf of authors, publishers, and readers on this predatory exploitation.
items.rationale: Official position statement from Europe's writers' federation calling on EU policymakers to act on destructive book scanning for AI training; primary source, new institutional action.

items.title: In New York, a small library's 'Bye Bye AI' event to remove AI features goes viral
items.excerpt: A public library in upstate New York has gone viral for offering an unusual kind of tech assistance: helping people switch off AI features on their phones and computers.
items.rationale: Concrete library program helping patrons switch off AI features; novel public-library response to AI not seen in history.

items.title: Book-smart and shelf aware: How AI and bots are changing libraries
items.excerpt: Around the world, shelf-reading bots and AI cataloguing are changing the way we borrow from libraries. What does this mean for a millennia-old institution?
items.rationale: Survey of deployed shelf-reading robots and AI cataloguing in libraries (e.g. Singapore NLB); concrete tooling rather than policy debate.

https://europeanwriterscouncil.eu/ewc-de.new_action: European Writers Council issued a formal statement condemning destructive book scanning for AI training and calling on European decision-makers to act (new institutional release, not further reporting on the scanning itself).
